correctness.rationale: For all \(n\ge2\), identify vectors with Eulerian walks in the four-state order-two de Bruijn graph; the strong connectivity criterion is weak connectedness of the positive-edge support plus the zero or single-source-single-sink flow imbalance. Unique imbalance gives exactly 13 disjoint cases. Separate isolated self-loops, use exact support inclusion-exclusion on the six nonloop arcs and their incident loop allowances, then parametrize integer flows by (b,c,d). The four cases for c,f yield a rational series through elementary geometric sums; a common denominator \(D_0=(1-z)^3(1-z^2)(1-z^3)(1-z^4)\) and the explicit summation bounds prove \(D_0H\) has degree at most 28. The supplied standalone checker independently hashes all actual word vectors to length 16, enumerates flows to 40 reads, and exhaustively verifies the degree-28 polynomial identity, obtaining the exact claimed P. Cyclotomic noncancellation and the pole at one give minimal period 12 and \(13/288\) asymptotics. No finite-only inference is used.

value.rationale: The exact number of distinguishable read-multiplicity outputs is the natural optimal zero-error code size for a full binary fixed-3-mer multiset observation model. Earlier literature emphasizes asymptotics, codes and constrained balanced vectors. The theorem gives the complete infinite length-by-length invariant, a concise rational generating function, an exact period-twelve refinement and a structural flow/connectivity proof rather than a numerical table. The binary length-three specialization is the first nontrivial four-vertex de Bruijn graph, not an arbitrarily selected parameter slice.
